title: New Orleans clubs he visited
summary: He recalls the Rhythm Club, Gypsy Tea Room, Hi-Hat, Club Astoria and eating grits and liver at Uncle Dan's.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: A couple of questions about some clubs. Did you ever go to the Rhythm Club? Did you know the Rhythm Club?

I went to the Rhythm Club one time. I went to see Jay McShane. And I brought my cousin. My cousin, he and his wife, they had a little spat. I said, come on man, you need to get away from this kind of stuff. So he and I, we went back to the Rhythm Club back on Jackson Avenue. Right. There was another club back on the Coliseum.
We went also, it was the Gypsy Tea Room.
Let's see, I can't remember all the clubs man.
The time's in the past. I can't remember all those places anymore.

But they tore all that stuff down to build what they have today. Yeah. What they have over there now. Yeah. The Hi-Hat, I think it was another club. The Santa Santa was another club. Then there was one on Rampart Street. I can't remember that. It was very famous, very popular one time.
It was Astoria? I don't remember that.

Yeah. Yeah. And I went basically all those clubbing one time or another. But it's been so long ago man, I can't remember. Then whenever we'd go out, we'd always end up our Uncle Dan's on La Salle Street, go and get some food. Yeah. He was known for his grits and liver. stuff
